newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dlr stable after bank-speculator jousting.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dlr stable after bank-speculator jousting.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar eased into range trading against the U.S. dollar at mid-session on Tuesday after a spate of jousting between the central bank and offshore speculators seeking a stronger greenback, dealers said.

The Taiwan dollar slumped at the open to T$27.935, below its eight-year closing low, but the central bank's stout defence sapped speculative interest and by 0400 GMT had muscled the currency back to T$27.912 against Monday's T$27.909 finish.
Turnover through dealers was a modest US$157 million.
Dealers said overseas speculators had sought to test the bank's bottom line for the recently sinking Taiwan dollar.
Dealers said the central bank defence worked.
"The central bank made it clear it would not permit the Taiwan dollar to fall so fast, and hence trading returned to normal," said one dealer at a foreign bank.

Taiwan's currency has been on a slow decline since early 1997, with senior analysts polled by Reuters forecasting that the rate would slip to T$28 to the U.S. dollar in the second half -- but only when the central bank is ready.
Dealers said they expected the rate to remain in a consolidation on Tuesday afternoon.
-- Kevin Chen, Taipei Newsroom (886-2-5080815) (c) Reuters Limited 1997
